- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.5) or volatile, model often underestimates or overshoots after sharp spikes; dampen early peaks.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent price spikes (e.g., +5–10% in 1–2 days) — cap forecast rise to 3–5% above prior peak unless sentiment confirms continuation.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline after peak), model often fails to adjust — reduce forecast by 1–2% per day of reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate mid-term trends when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive — apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% if sentiment < 0.6.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.8 → -0.7 → +0.2), model often misreads momentum — adjust forecast to align with sentiment swing direction, not trend.
